note: DAN.1.6-7, the four are given their Babylonian names. This scene owns the dormitory of nine beds on the precinct's west side; the palace front (scene 3), the food pavilion (scene 5), the terraced garden (scene 6) and the ziggurat/scribal quarter (scene 7) are left untouched. This is a roll-call at the trainees' own quarters rather than a public ceremony, so the registry table sits among the beds rather than at the palace door. The registry scribe is the focal point, pressing each new name into the clay; Ashpenaz stands over his shoulder, the one actually conferring the names. Daniel and Hananiah are brought to the table first; Mishael and Azariah wait their turn down the west aisle between the beds, with a trainee further back at the tail of the same line, so the queue bends around the dormitory rather than reading as a straight row of four. The exit is the palace doorway gap, the same door scene 3 uses, leading on to scene 5's dinner table.
